findings.message: apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts keeps a module-level `outcomes: MatchOutcome[]` array. `endMatch` pushes every finished match's full MatchResults onto it and never removes any, including in the production entry (DEFAULT_MATCH_TUNING, main.ts). `recordedOutcomes()` is only read by tests and diagnostics. So a long-running production server's memory grows by one entry for every match it ever finishes. The fix is to bound it (a ring buffer, or a test-only switch like `testHooks`) or hand outcomes to a store and drop them.

A UI branch this feature added is missing from docs/match-online-coverage.md and has no test. In apps/web/src/flowHud.ts showBanner (line 647), `if (timers.hide !== undefined) window.clearTimeout(timers.hide)` re-arms the banner's 7 s hide when a new reveal arrives. The banner's auto-hide after BANNER_MS isn't asserted anywhere either. fullMatch.spec.ts only checks that the banner is hidden before the first reveal and visible after it. The host gets final-route and final-sector a few ms apart, so deleting the clearTimeout would fail no test. Add a table row and a test (for example a DOM unit test with fake timers: a second banner inside 7 s stays up for its own 7 s).

# Decisions: match-online-fixes-2

From the operator session of 2026-09-25, decided by the assistant under the operator's standing instruction and recorded in `operator-logs/decisions-overnight.md`.

## Decisions

- match-online-fixes-001 passed every check. Its coverage reviewer blocked it on a missing branch table, untested player-id filters and untested DOM rendering branches, and its general reviewer was stopped before a verdict. This follow-up restores its snapshot (`ac3a5e8`) on the same base, so the whole feature is reviewed again.
- The branch table is a committed file (`docs/match-online-coverage.md`), not only report text, so reviewers can check it against the code.
- "Unreachable" isn't an accepted state: a defensive branch is tested through an extracted pure function or the room, or removed if it's dead code.
- DOM rendering is made testable by moving its decisions into pure view models. The no-winner results headline for the deadline gets the new browser scenario `match-deadline`. The abandoned and aborted headlines are covered by the view-model unit tests.

## Assumptions

- Everything in `features/match-online/` and `features/match-online-fixes/` stands.

## Deferred

- `ruins-online` comes next.

concerns.message: `match-deadline` has to watch the timer run out inside Playwright's 60 s per-test timeout. But match timings are set per server process, not per match: `MatchTuning` goes in through `startGameServer({ matchTuning })` and `dev.ts` env vars, and the e2e config starts one server with one env for every spec. The shortened match duration that `full-match` needs (ready countdown, two 6 s collections, sailing, a 10 s claim) is probably longer than a deadline you can wait out cheaply. The task doesn't say how the new scenario gets its own shorter deadline.
concerns.consequence: Shortening the deadline for the whole server can end `full-match`, `theft-loop` or `sea-duel` mid-test. The quick alternative, a per-match timing option on create or join that the client controls, would be a new test-only setting the room reads, so it could reach production. If you instead wait out the shared duration, the scenario needs `test.setTimeout` and makes the browser suite longer. Each path adds rows to the branch table and gives the reviewer something new to flag.

concerns.message: The scenario says the compass is 'shown inactive while no route is known'. Finding 3, though, talks about 'an inactive or absent compass' as separate cases, and the settled design shows the compass only to the holder and makes the route inactive only after a type is lost. In `match-deadline` nobody collects anything, so under a three-state model (absent / inactive / active) the page would be in `absent`, not `inactive`.
concerns.consequence: The worker either asserts `data-compass=absent` against a description that says 'inactive' (the reviewer blocks on the mismatch), or quietly merges absent into inactive and shows a compass to non-holders. That second option changes the settled UI and loses a view-model branch the unit tests are supposed to separate.

concerns.message: 'Delete the branch' has no fixed meaning for guards and filters. Removing an `if` body, forcing its condition true, and forcing it false give different mutants. The unknown-id filters, the join-refused backstop and the checks that keep test-only settings off by default each have two meaningful deletions. The table format (file/function, branch, test) has no column that records which mutation was run.
concerns.consequence: Rows can't be reproduced: the reviewer tries the other mutation, no test fails, and the feature goes into a third review round. The 'test-only setting is never read by production' rows are the likeliest to have no failing test for the 'always on' mutation.

concerns.message: 'Every room-level and UI branch this feature added or changed' has no mechanical scope. The listed categories alone come to roughly 40–60 rows (9 results columns, 5 claim resets, 4 endings, 4 reveals, 3+ test-only settings, seeds, lobby/late-join/ready/control, the filter drops, the view-model branches), and some rows can only be proved by browser specs that rebuild Vite on every run.
concerns.consequence: Building the table by hand-mutating each row is slow: there are many integration and Playwright runs against the 171.6 s suite and a per-run Vite build. If it's under-scoped, the reviewer finds an unlisted branch in the feature diff and blocks again, which is the same loop this run is meant to end.

concerns.message: To do the room-level ghost-id test through the real room, the worker would have to add a hook that injects a report, since players can't produce an unknown id through their own input. The task also allows 'a unit test that builds the room's flow step'.
concerns.consequence: A new injection hook on `MatchRoom` is one more test-only surface. It needs its own gating, its own row and its own proof that production doesn't read it, and it conflicts with 'tests drive input like players do'. Testing the exported `stepFlowWith` (or its extracted pure core) directly avoids all of that.

concerns.message: Mutation runs of UI or test-setting branches on a scratch copy need Playwright, and the e2e config binds fixed ports 2593/5393 with `reuseExistingServer: false`. The machine is shared by several runs.
concerns.consequence: A scratch-copy browser run that overlaps with the worker's own run, or another run's, fails to start because the port is taken. That reads as 'the mutant was killed', so the table gets a false row.

challenge.simpler_alternative:
Keep the plan's shape and cut the moving parts:
- **Ghost-id test and backstop:** unit-test the extracted `knownFlowReports`, and prove the room-level case by calling the room's exported flow step with a ghost id. Don't add a report-injection hook to `MatchRoom`. If admission (`onAuth`/`onJoin`) already refuses late joiners, remove the join-refused backstop as dead code, with its reason in the table.
- **`match-deadline`:** give it a longer `test.setTimeout` and let it wait out the e2e server's existing shortened match duration. Change the one server-wide env duration only if that wait is unreasonable. Don't add a per-match timing option that clients control.
- **Branch table:** scope it mechanically. Take the conditionals on added lines in the feature diff (`git diff 539b6de ac3a5e8 -- apps`) plus the listed categories. Add a column for the mutation applied to each branch (body removed / condition forced true / condition forced false), so a reviewer can re-run any row.
challenge.cheap_experiment:
This takes about two minutes and needs no code change. It shows whether `match-deadline` can share the one e2e server and whether 'inactive' is the right state to assert:
- Run `git show ac3a5e8:tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts | grep -n ENV\|env` and `git show ac3a5e8:apps/server/src/dev.ts | grep -n -i 'duration\|ready\|deadline'`. This shows how the e2e server shortens the match and ready durations and to what values. If the match duration is server-wide and longer than about 45 s, you need a longer per-test timeout or a second tuning path.
- Run `git show ac3a5e8:apps/web/src/seaScene.ts | grep -n -A25 drawTreasure` and `git show ac3a5e8:apps/web/src/flowHud.ts | grep -n -i 'inactive\|route\|compass'`. This shows whether the snapshot tells 'no route yet' apart from 'route lost'. If it does, the scenario's 'shown inactive' wording has to be settled first, before any code is written.

3. **(P2) The rendering branches.** Split `renderFlow` and `drawTreasure` into a pure view model (the text, visibility and state flags per element) and a thin applier with no branches of its own. Assert these on the page (text and `data-*` state), not just on the model.

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json` (which adds `docs/match-online-coverage.md`). Apart from restoring the snapshot, change only what the findings need. Keep the structure, names, every scenario id and every existing test.
- Tests drive input like players do.
- Keep the integration suite well inside its 300 s budget (the last run took 171.6 s). The new browser scenario uses test-only short timings; it must not wait out a real 35-minute clock.

- The restored feature meets all of `features/match-online/game-task.md`'s acceptance and `features/match-online-fixes/game-task.md`'s findings 1–4.

scenarios.description: One browser creates a private match from the landing page; the HUD shows the code, the protocol version, one player and a connected status.
Two browsers join the same private match with their ships in sight of each other; one sails with the keyboard and the other browser's view shows that ship at the new server-authoritative position.
A browser sails its ship around a shoal to an island dock with the keyboard and docks there; the HUD shows the dock and the ship stops at it.
Two browsers in one match with their ships out of sight of each other: neither view lists or draws the other ship until one sails within the sight radius, and it disappears again when it sails away.

One browser opens a practice duel against the dummy, lands a jab and then a keyboard throw (J then K a frame apart); the dummy's health bar and the HUD drop by the move data's damage, and hitboxes can be shown.

Two browsers: one creates a duel, the other joins by its code; after the countdown the first lands a strike on the second, and both views show the same authoritative health, round clock and result, with the connection line showing input delay and corrections.

Two browsers in one match are placed within grapple range; the host sails at the guest and presses J; both see the grapple telegraph, then a three-second countdown and the arena; the duel is decided; the winner returns to the sea with protection shown, and the loser sees a respawn countdown and then their ship at a dock.

Two browsers moored at different islands each hold E and collect a different rubbing type; the host grapples the guest at sea, wins the duel by tapping attack keys, and picks the guest's type within five seconds; the host's HUD shows both types and more gold, the guest's shows the loss.

Two browsers: the host starts a private match from the lobby, both see the ready countdown and the match timer; the host collects both rubbing types, sees the full-set reveal and the route, sails to the final island's claim tile and holds E for ten seconds; both browsers show the results with the host as the winner.

Two browsers start a private match from the lobby with test-only short timings; nobody claims; the timer runs out; both browsers show the results with the no-winner deadline headline, and the route compass is shown inactive while no route is known.
